Data efficiency

Dataset condensation for time-series learning

Dual-domain gradient matching produced a compact synthetic set that achieved 82.5 percent evaluation accuracy using four percent of the original data.

At a glance

Keep the information, not every example.

Time seriesSynthetic dataPyTorchEvaluation
Problem

Large time-series datasets increase storage, iteration time, and compute cost. Standard condensation methods built for images can miss spectral structure that distinguishes temporal signals.

Method

The implementation reproduces dual-domain dataset condensation by matching training gradients in both time and frequency domains. It evaluates Human Activity Recognition data and Synthetic Control Chart sequences to test both multi-channel motion and global temporal shapes.

Result

A synthetic set containing four percent of the original examples supported 82.5 percent test accuracy—a 25× reduction while retaining much of the decision structure. The repository includes the report, training code, loaders, and plot generation.

Takeaway

Efficient learning is not only about smaller models. Better-chosen training data can reduce the cost of experiments and deployment pipelines while preserving useful temporal and spectral information.
